policy: Borrow useful mechanisms and build credited matched controls; overlapping components do not close an idea. No independent originality or reproduced speed claim.

papers.title: Sparse Inter-Layer Dependencies of Transformer FFN Neurons
papers.inspected: Sections3,4.1-4.3,5.3,5.5; author paper, not repository code
papers.useful_primitive: Center upstream residual contributions and retain their normalization denominator in attribution.
papers.original_regime: Language-model activation attribution and mean ablations; model-level perplexity interventions, not native Wan FFN latency.
papers.adaptation_cost: Upstream contribution storage/readout must be charged. Start with scalar residual statistics rather than a dense dependency matrix.
papers.overlap: Pre-W1 upstream information and normalization geometry; no claim that these ingredients are new.
papers.distinctive_prediction: Residual scale adds finite compensated-action information conditional on current normalized input; activation prediction alone need not improve decisions.
papers.matched_baseline: Current-input-only predictor and fixed position policy at identical inference budget.

papers.title: PulseQuant
papers.inspected: Sections4.1-4.2, isolated-pulse definition and Eq4-7; author paper
papers.useful_primitive: Same-prefix finite intervention followed by continued denoising measures propagation risk.
papers.original_regime: Offline video W4 calibration, row-radius selection and code corrections; exported packed quantized weights.
papers.adaptation_cost: Offline counterfactual continuations; selecting FFN computation online needs separately measured routing and kernel costs.
papers.overlap: Propagation-sensitive error and response correction are established useful components.
papers.distinctive_prediction: Actual compensated channel-action preferences vary with affordable pre-W1 state beyond a block-step risk table.
papers.matched_baseline: Fixed block-step propagation weighting with the same complete actions.

papers.title: Prox
papers.inspected: Sections4.1-4.3, two-stage mask and implementation descriptions; author paper
papers.useful_primitive: Use an inexpensive proxy only to select a mask, then execute retained channels with original weights.
papers.original_regime: LLM SwiGLU and single-batch decoding; INT4 proxy kernels, three projections.
papers.adaptation_cost: Wan has two GELU projections, many parallel tokens and frozen HiF4. Proxy, grouping and compaction need native timing.
papers.overlap: Cheap channel prediction and exact selected computation; suitable credited comparator.
papers.distinctive_prediction: Predicting compensated downstream gain outperforms magnitude selection at equal physical cost.
papers.matched_baseline: Adapted magnitude proxy with the identical whole64-group action set and compensation.

papers.title: FastForward
papers.inspected: Official abstract only in this continuation; earlier method card remains historical
papers.useful_primitive: Combine block-context prediction, error compensation and layer compute allocation.
papers.original_regime: LLM prefill, language-model accuracy and time-to-first-token.
papers.adaptation_cost: Predictor and compensation must share native video precision, support and complete FFN budget.
papers.overlap: Predictor-plus-compensator is a prior building block, not an independent novelty claim.
papers.distinctive_prediction: Adding residual-scale information improves complete-action decision regret over a current-input predictor.
papers.matched_baseline: Current-input block predictor with identical compensation and capacity.

papers.title: Temporal Aware Pruning for Efficient Diffusion-based Video Generation
papers.inspected: Official abstract only in this continuation
papers.useful_primitive: Smooth importance temporally and reselect by layer to reduce persistent selection errors.
papers.original_regime: Video token pruning and denoising budget scheduling.
papers.adaptation_cost: Temporal smoothing, sorting and reindexing count toward actual FFN cost; latent bins differ from decoded frames.
papers.overlap: Temporal coherence and mask stability are established controls.
papers.distinctive_prediction: Useful temporal selection requires improved propagated quality, not merely a lower mask-flip count.
papers.matched_baseline: Regular time pattern and smoothed selection with equal executed dense-row count.

papers.title: Output-aware Residual Stream Pruning for Large Language Models
papers.inspected: Sections4,4.1 and shared-curvature discussion around Eq3; author paper, newly found search result
papers.useful_primitive: Weight perturbation directions by output sensitivity rather than activation energy alone.
papers.original_regime: Static rotated residual-dimension pruning with an output-KL approximation.
papers.adaptation_cost: Full curvature is expensive. Compare a fixed shared metric with direct finite-action labels before considering a conditional approximation.
papers.overlap: Direction-sensitive downstream objectives are established, including loss of activation-curvature correlations under sharing.
papers.distinctive_prediction: Affordable state predicts action preferences that disappear under a dataset-shared downstream metric.
papers.matched_baseline: Shared sensitivity metric and position-only action values.

papers.title: SVG-EAR
papers.inspected: Official abstract only; newly found adjacent-domain source
papers.useful_primitive: Compensate skipped contributions cheaply and spend exact computation on compensation error per unit cost.
papers.original_regime: Clustered sparse video attention with centroid compensation; not FFN sparsity.
papers.adaptation_cost: FFN compensation-error estimation must avoid omitted dense W1; attention formulas cannot be transplanted unchanged.
papers.overlap: Exact exceptions should target compensation failure rather than raw contribution magnitude.
papers.distinctive_prediction: The error remaining AFTER R256, rather than R256 energy itself, predicts useful FFN exceptions.
papers.matched_baseline: R16 residual-energy selection at matched real cost, where comparable.

papers.title: MC-Sparse
papers.inspected: Official abstract only; newly found adjacent-domain source
papers.useful_primitive: Separate grouping constraints, selection errors and omitted-contribution errors using physically executable oracles.
papers.original_regime: Sparse attention, query groups, selected KV tokens and metadata reuse across denoising.
papers.adaptation_cost: Four-step distillation limits reuse. FFN group/tile layout and cache invalidation require independent validation.
papers.overlap: Hardware-aligned grouping and compensation are useful comparators, not new ingredients.
papers.distinctive_prediction: A matched FFN oracle must use executable compensated group bundles; post-hoc output mosaics overstate feasible action freedom.
papers.matched_baseline: Best fixed physically identical bundle and oracle on exactly that bundle set.
